sentence: Warfarin is an anticoagulant, often called a blood thinner, used to prevent and treat blood clots.
note: NHS page title: medicine used to prevent and treat blood clots.

sentence: It does not literally thin the blood; it makes clots form less readily.
note: Not stated in returned text; plain-language textbook explanation.

sentence: Because it lowers the chance of clots, the main risk that comes with it is bleeding.
note: NHS: the main side effect of warfarin is an increased risk of bleeding.

sentence: People on warfarin are given an anticoagulant alert card because of the bleeding risk.
note: NHS: you will be given an anticoagulant alert card because warfarin may put you at risk of bleeding.

sentence: Which clots and conditions it is prescribed for is a decision for the specialist or GP who starts it.
note: NHS page framed as prescribed medicine; no condition list retrieved beyond preventing and treating clots.

sentence: Regular blood tests measure how quickly the blood clots, and the result guides the warfarin dose.
note: Search summary of NHS: regular tests measure clotting and dose is adjusted from the results.

sentence: This test is called the international normalised ratio, or INR.
note: Summary: called an INR test.

sentence: Testing is usually more frequent while the right dose is being found.
note: Existing page and NHS dosage page describe frequent early checks; search summary on INR said results fluctuate.

sentence: The main side effect of warfarin is an increased risk of bleeding.
note: NHS: main side effect is increased risk of bleeding.

sentence: Unexplained bruising is among the signs that people are usually advised to report to their anticoagulant service or GP.
note: Search summary: warfarin users usually advised to report unexplained bruising to anticoagulant service or GP.

sentence: Other signs of bleeding listed by NHS sources include blood in the urine or poo, black poo, nosebleeds, coughing or vomiting blood, and heavy periods.
note: Summary: bleeding signs listed include blood in urine or stools (red or black), nosebleeds, coughing or vomiting blood, heavy periods.

sentence: The NHS says to call NHS 111 if there are signs of bleeding, after a head injury, or if another serious side effect is suspected.
note: Summary of NHS warfarin page: urgent advice, call NHS 111 if symptoms of bleeding, head injury, or another serious side effect.

sentence: Heavy bleeding that will not stop needs a 999 call or A&E.
note: Summary: heavy or uncontrolled bleeding warrants emergency response (one leaflet said dial 999).

sentence: A sudden severe headache with confusion, slurred speech or weakness in a limb can signal bleeding in the brain or a stroke and needs a 999 call.
note: Summary: sudden severe headache with confusion, slurred speech or limb weakness can signal bleeding in the brain; stroke signs need 999.

sentence: A painful skin rash can be a sign of a rare condition called calciphylaxis, and a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) is an emergency; both are listed on the NHS page.
note: Summary: NHS page lists painful skin rash as possible calciphylaxis and severe allergic reaction, needing urgent help.

sentence: Foods rich in vitamin K, such as leafy greens, broccoli, liver and chickpeas, affect how warfarin works.
note: Summary: vitamin K foods such as leafy greens, broccoli, liver, chickpeas affect warfarin.

sentence: They do not need to be avoided; the NHS stresses eating a consistent amount so the clinic can adjust the dose to match.
note: Summary: don't need to avoid; important to be consistent in amount.

sentence: Cranberry juice and grapefruit juice are best avoided because they can increase the blood-thinning effect.
note: Summary: avoid cranberry and grapefruit juice; NHS says they can increase blood-thinning effect.

sentence: The NHS anticoagulant guidance says binge drinking should never happen on warfarin, and that regular drinking should stay modest.
note: Summary: NHS anticoagulant guidance on alcohol: modest daily amount, never binge drink (figures omitted).

sentence: The NHS says some medicines, remedies and supplements may not mix well with warfarin, so a doctor should know about everything else a person takes.
note: Summary: some medicines, remedies and supplements may not mix well; tell your doctor.

sentence: Antibiotics, antidepressants, steroids, anticonvulsants and anti-inflammatory painkillers such as ibuprofen can affect anticoagulants.
note: Summary: antibiotics, antidepressants, steroids, anticonvulsants and NSAIDs such as ibuprofen can affect anticoagulants.

sentence: Herbal products also matter, and St John's wort in particular is not taken with warfarin.
note: Summary: St John's wort must not be taken with warfarin.

sentence: Sickness or diarrhoea can change the INR, so the anticoagulant clinic is told about illness as well as new medicines.
note: Summary: illness with vomiting or diarrhoea can change INR; contact clinic (from NHS trust leaflets).

sentence: The NHS says most people can take warfarin, but it is not suitable for everyone.
note: Summary: most can take it but not suitable for everyone.

sentence: Extra care or a different treatment may be needed with an allergy to warfarin, liver or kidney problems, high blood pressure, a recent stroke, recent or planned surgery, or conditions that raise bleeding risk such as a stomach ulcer.
note: Summary lists these conditions.

sentence: Warfarin is not usually used in pregnancy because it can affect the baby's development, though it is sometimes used after the doctor discusses risks and benefits.
note: Summary: not usually used in pregnancy as it can affect baby's development; can be used sometimes.

sentence: The NHS advises telling a doctor straight away about a pregnancy or plans to conceive, and not stopping warfarin unless told to.
note: Summary: tell doctor straight away; don't stop unless told.

sentence: The NHS says warfarin can usually be taken while breastfeeding, after discussing it with a GP or midwife first.
note: Summary: usually can take while breastfeeding; discuss first.

sentence: Not literally. Warfarin is called a blood thinner, but it works by making clots form less readily. The NHS describes it as a medicine used to prevent and treat blood clots, and says its main side effect is an increased risk of bleeding.
note: NHS title/summary: prevents and treats clots; main side effect bleeding. 'Not literally' is textbook.

sentence: It is a card given to people on warfarin because the medicine may put them at risk of bleeding.
note: NHS: given an anticoagulant alert card because warfarin may put you at risk of bleeding. Who it informs is the existing page's text.

sentence: The NHS says to call NHS 111 after a head injury while on warfarin, as well as for any signs of bleeding. Sudden severe headache with confusion, slurred speech or weakness in a limb needs a 999 call, as it can signal bleeding in the brain or a stroke.
note: Summary of NHS warfarin page: call 111 for bleeding, head injury; headache/confusion/slurred speech/limb weakness emergency.

sentence: No. Leafy greens, broccoli, liver and chickpeas are rich in vitamin K and affect warfarin, but the NHS stresses eating a consistent amount rather than avoiding them, so the clinic can adjust the dose. Cranberry juice and grapefruit juice are the drinks to avoid.
note: Summary: don't need to avoid; consistent; avoid cranberry and grapefruit juice.

sentence: The NHS says warfarin is not usually used in pregnancy because it can affect the baby's development, although it is sometimes used after the doctor talks through risks and benefits. Anyone pregnant or planning a pregnancy is advised to tell their doctor straight away and not to stop it unless told to.
note: Summary of NHS warfarin page on pregnancy.

sentence: Anticoagulant (blood thinner) taken to prevent and treat blood clots
note: NHS title.

sentence: Bleeding, which is why an anticoagulant alert card is given
note: NHS: main side effect bleeding; alert card.

sentence: Regular INR blood tests guide the dose
note: Summary: regular tests measure clotting; dose adjusted; called INR.

sentence: Keep vitamin K foods consistent; avoid cranberry and grapefruit juice
note: Summary of NHS food advice.

sentence: 999 for heavy bleeding or stroke signs; NHS 111 for signs of bleeding or a head injury
note: Summary of NHS urgent advice.

sentence: Not usually used; sometimes used after risks and benefits are discussed
note: Summary of NHS pregnancy advice.
